tips.comment: Ralph Beckett's unbeaten Amiloc looks the one to be with. Not the most straitforward, as his dam was somewhat tricky & looked to be going nowhere in the Goodwood Listed race he won last month, but once hitting the mile pole, he just took off to run out an easy 4l winner. This extra furlong can only help & I don't think connections know how good he is yet.

2000 Guineas third Shadow Of Light looks the one to be on dropping down to six furlongs. The form was boosted by the first two home in the St James Palace on Tuesday & the Appleby/Godolphin runner looks the best bet for Friday's card

4/10 winning favs, 6/10 top 3 in the betting. 8/10 rated 113+. 8/10 had a Group win. Beat WHistlejacket twice now, the first in the Phoenix STakes G1 on GF. Followed that up with 4.75L 4th to Lake VIctoria on Soft, form that has been very strongly boosted. Looked abit lost on Listed return however was expected to come on for the run and duly did so beating Whistlejacket agin to win the G3 Lacken Stakes by 2.75L, looked ery smart there and whilst its obvious SHadow Of Light is the main danger, would expect to be around in the finish and could notch another win for Juddmonte

BIG MOJO brings the recent Ascot fast ground six furlong winning form which can only read well. A progressive three year old sprinter with a noteworthy sire and ace jockey Hollie Doyle rides the straight course at least as well as any other. Value shout.

There are several strong contenders in what looks a red-hot renewal of the Commonwealth Cup, but I get the feeling that bookmakers may be underestimating the French Aga Khan filly Rayevka, who appears to have taken a major step forward from two to three. She produced what looked like a Group 1-level performance last time out at Chantilly under Mickael Barzalona. Although that was “only” a Listed contest, it was run at a strong gallop, and from the side-angle camera you could see her travelling powerfully before unleashing an impressive turn of foot to settle matters quickly. While the ground was officially described as good to soft, the race time suggests it was quicker, something that often goes under the radar in French racing. The fact she’s been supplemented for this race signals clear intent, and with a likely strong early pace at Ascot, she should get the perfect tow into the contest. The stiff finish should suit her well, and Francis Graffard’s yard is in flying form back home. At 25/1, with some firms offering 5 places, she looks a very interesting each-way bet who could pick up the pieces late.

Most of these horse will be in the improvement stage so i don't think the official ratings are much to go by.
Instead I will look at connections and previous race graded.
This horse won twice in group 2 and 3 races as a two year old and returned on the all weather with a solid effort in a hot conditions races.
That will have sharpened him up for a tilt at this race today which may well.have been the longer term target.
Big race at big odds expected.

There are some potential superstars in here including Shadow Of Light and Jonquil but the former is short enough for me and the latter I suspect will appreciate slower ground. The pace and the market leaders are all drawn high and amongst them I think Leovanni is being massively overlooking. She won the Queen Mary over 5f here on rattling ground last year and was given a very easy time of things on return when still finishing 4th in a Listed race at Haydock - the winner that day ran pretty well in the King Charles Stakes on Tuesday. Had excuses last season following her win here, with the ground far too soft at Newmarket. Gets her ideal conditions here and looks to have a perfect draw - way too big a price.

Has nice low draw from stall 3 last 3 winners have all come from stall 4 & lower . Dons visor for 1st time after a decent 2nd here over CD beaten 0.5L to fellow rival Big Mojo 51 days ago . Has a bit to find on ratings but could bag a place at big odds .

Realign is the proverbial group horse in a handicap and can win this before bigger targets later this year. Finished 2L 2nd to Commonwealth Cup fav Shadow Of Light on debut over 6f, before 3rd stepping up to 7f in a competitive maiden at York (Oaks 2nd Whirl back in 5th). Reappeared over 6f with an easy victory in a Salisbury maiden and dropping to sprinting strips should be much better than his opening mark of 93. Fast ground with suit and draw looks fine, giving him options both sides. Had his own Group 1 entry this meeting but connections aim for the low hanging fruit.

This is going to be run at a very fast pace and normally i'd exclude fornt runners here however the Chester run was very impressive to my eye. Rubys profit Led there, since won at Goodwood and ran a huge race in the 3yo Dash to lead and hang on for 3rd, its a diffuclt course to make all Epsom and there was plenty trying to force the pace, everything else in the first 6 had come from behind. Redorange managing to pass that one around Chester where theres such an advantage for front runners is clearly good form. The 3rd that day also finished 4th in the 3yo Dash. CLive Cox spoke highly post race and elected this as the target. Also said hed be much better on a Firmer surface with it being on the Softer side of Good that day. Low draw could pose a problem but may be too classy. Have backed EW

Finished 4th in Group 2 Queen Mary in 2024 meeting & then won Listed on soft at Naas the run after . Been a little below par in 4 runs since running in Group 2 to Listed level class , has decent high draw here & back here could perform better than of late .

Looks a big price for a horse from this yard previously racing with credit in pattern races dropping into this handicap.
Arrives in good form after two good races so far this year so should be sharp enough to place at least.

Likely to be ran at a very fast pace this and a collapse is highly likely. That should sui this one as always likes to come from the back. Draw is solid. Has ran a few good races this year and was on the go Dec- April, given a break since. Run the last day at Sandown was a nice run, pace collapsed and set up well and would have won had he not jumped the path, going down by 0.5L. Redorange in 3rd there which has worked out well. SHould set up to suit and is a nice price ew here with 6 and 7 places around.

The French Guineas winner, (awarded the race in the stewards room), looks easily the form pick here & if continuing her improvement will be hard to beat. Her trainer won this with a similar type in 2019.

She's undefeated in all of her 3 runs & is steadily progressing after 2 wins on the all weather at Wolverhampton over 7f & Kempton over 8f she then won Listed at York over today's trip by 0.5L staying on strongly as the end .

The Coronation Stakes seems to lack a superstar at this stage, with no Desert Flower, Lake Victoria or last years winner Porta Fortuna lining up. The French horse has a quirk or two and I'm not sure about the ground, and whilst Falakeyah was mightily impressive they were fairly modest horses in behind that day. Simmering has saved her best for quick ground and Ascot, having chased home Fairy Godmother over 6f in the Albany last year before winning a pair of Group races, first here at Ascot and then at Deauville. Put her reappearance behind her when finishing a good 3rd in the 1000 Guineas on fast ground before bombing out behind some of these in the Irish version. Trainer reaches for cheekpieces and if the headgear does its trick, a return to fast ground at Ascot should see her go very close in what looks a below par renewal.

Ran slow here however fron two came from the back so can be rated up. Starman filly and cost 260k gns at Craven Breeze Up. 3rd,4th and 6th have all won since so likely decent form. Was value for further than the winning margi there and should improve.

Won on debut at the Curragh over today's 6f trip & then 33 days ago finished 2nd in Group 3 Fillies only beaten 0.75L & staying on well at the business end & should come on & be stronger for that run .

10/12 4-5yo, 5/12 winning favs, 6/12 top 3 in the betting. 9/12 stall 12+. 7/12 won lto. 9/12 had 2 runs over 12 furlongs. 8/12 rated 95-102, 10/12 had a run this season. Bought by Wathnan after nice York Race To The Ebor win.Only ever does enough to win so makes it hard on the handicapper and also ahrd to judge where the ceiling is however is now 3 from 4, relatively unexposed and still appears to be improving. Ebor the end goal for the season so trip should hold no issues. Shouldnt be an overly strong pace here which would suit. SHould be around in the finish.

Hand Of God was a convincing winner of the Golden Gates handicap at this meeting last year, his final race of the season. His last run at the Guineas meeting at Newmarket, after 315 days off, can be forgiven & there's little doubt this race has been his target. The step up to 1m4f shouldn't be a problem as there's plenty of stamina in his pedigree.

This is drop down in class from last year when War Rooms ran in the Group 2 King Edward VII Stakes here following on from running at York in the Dante where he was 3rd, he moved from Owen Burrows to Gerard Keane in Ireland earlier this year after being gelded and has since run second twice over 14f beaten only a nose last time by San Salvador at Killarney. First time cheekpieces are applied and he drops back to 12f with Colin Keane on board.

Unexposed 4 year old who's only ran 8 times including a CD win back in July 2024 in class 2 on good . Has had 2 runs this season 4th at Kempton over 11f in March & then 43 days ago was 5th of 6 at Chester over 13.5f in Group 3 but was out of depth behind the likes of Illinois & SL Qareem but today's drop back to today's trip should suit .

My selection has improved no end since joining the Tom Dascombe yard, winning on debut at Bath by an impressive 8.5 lengths, before upped in grade (this level) and finishing a fine looking 4th of 23 in the November handicap at Doncaster last year. Had an all-weather listed run in Dec 3rd of 6 before being put away . Reappeared in a 10f class 2 at Chester when beaten a head after being denied a clear run. Comes from a smaller unfashionable yard and if with another bigger one would be single figure odds for sure.

5/12 winning favs, 7/12 top 3 in the betting. 8/12 won lto. 9/12 rated 91+. Should be going pretty quick here which would suit those coming from further back, a style she likes to employ. Very impressive dbut at Haydock on heavy, didnt follow up the next time when beat 17L in a Newbury Listed race. Was presumably something amiss there as returned in good form coming from the rear to easily win a class 3 2.25L from Treasure in 2nd whos held somegood form, namely running to within 1.75L of You Got To Me in the Linfield Oaks Trial, she subsequently won the Irish Oaks and finished 2nd in the Yorkshire equivelent. Looks the type to run well in these sort of handicaps and with 6 places around is the bet ew.

The Sandringham Stakes looks typically competitive, with the market opening at 8/1 the field in a 28-runner lineup. There are plenty of lightly raced, unexposed types who could be well ahead of their marks, but trying to pinpoint which ones is often a guessing game. Instead, I’m siding with proven form and selecting Betty Clover, who, despite already having ten runs to her name, makes her handicap debut only today. Eve Johnson Houghton’s filly has been campaigned exclusively in Group and Listed company, and arguably produced one of her best efforts here at Ascot last year, when narrowly beaten in a Group 3. She seems to have improved further for the step up in trip this season, going down by just a nose in a Listed race to the now Group 1-winning Crimson Advocate, before running another fine race to finish third in a Group 2 at Chantilly. Although more exposed than many rivals, I believe she brings a touch of class to this handicap and can use her experience to her advantage against lesser-tested opponents. At 12/1, with six places on offer from most bookmakers, she looks a solid each-way play.
Emma Lavelle's grey looked a big improver when easily winning at Goodwood last time & could well step-up for the extra furlong, giving the way she went clear last time.

Carthusian should be up to winning this maiden. He was second to Scandinavia, (who finished 5th not beaten far in a Group 2 at Ascot today), on his first run and with improvement can take this for his trainer Jessica Harrington who is in good form.

Happy Pharoah has 13 runs, wins, 5 places, so a 38% place rate. Trained by OBrien with Harnett riding, he is stepping up in trip and wearing a tongue tie for the first time. Stall 4 offers a decent draw for a forward run. He showed steady progress last time out over 10f and could improve here. A solid each way chance if he handles the step up and the pace stays honest

Mississippi River has strong form, with a win and two places in three runs at this distance, showing his suitability. His recent second at Naas, despite being the beaten favorite, was a solid effort, only 2½ lengths behind, and his prior handicap runner-up form has been franked, confirming his competitiveness.

Has been gelded since last seen in april. Has been consistent tihis year and just couldnt quite manage to follow up last time. Will be in the shake up here with connections putting up an experiemnced 5lb claimer

Won a maiden iover 1 mile at Yarmouth in a fast time last September for previous trainer. Finished well into 4th place over 7f at the Curragh on seasonal return last month when making debut for this trainer. Will prefer thisstep up to 1 mile and a top apprentice rides knocking off a handy 3lbs and looks a leading contender.
Was back to form last time at Fairyhouse when a close 2nd over 7f, beaten less than a length. This looks a tougher race but he should appreciate returning to a mile trip and worth considering.

is very lightly raced for his age and having been running over hurdles was switched to the flat at the Curragh the last twice over what would appear to be inadequate trips of 8f. Up significantly in trip here so expect a much stronger performance.
Had been running well over hurdles before switching to the flat last time at the Curragh where she finished a close up 5th over 12f. This extra distance will suit and she looks a strong contender.

Friary Road looks far to big a price in this maiden for older horses. He won bumpers at Listowel and Punchestown last October and although beaten in his next two starts they were at Listed and Graded level. He was second in a Dundalk maiden in February on Flat debut but that was only over 1m4f. The step up to 1m7f should suit and he can go well at big odds

This fairly useful handicapper has posted four respectable finishes on his last four starts. The latest here over 9f when failing to justify favouritism from a lb lower mark than racing off today. Deserves a change of fortune and won’t be far away.
Faoladh ran a super race to be second over C&D last week, only beaten by a short head. He's still lightly raced at this trip on good ground and can break his maiden today.

Stayed on well from the back of the field to finsih 5th of 18 over this CD 13 days ago from a wide draw given too much to do. The form has been biisted by the winner going in again and Tilani runs here off the same marl and could go close if able to lay up closer to the pace tonight.
Ransom won at the Curragh last month. Was beaten a short head over course and distance recently and has a chance.

Methgal looks interesting at a big price in this 8 furlongs Leopardstown handicap. Trained in Britain by Karl Burke as a two year old he was far from disgraced in two decent maidens at Haydock and Goodwood before finishing 3rd at Ayr. Although unplaced in both starts since moving to Ireland he only faded late on last week at Cork and with cheek pieces added for the first time he is worth a small EW bet with 5 places on offer

HAUGHTY runs for a shrewd dual-purpose operation and this five year old mare could be interesting back racing on the level given her early career flat form in Britain. She will not come undone with this turf handicap mark , so she merits a market check.

The price looks fair at 33/1 for Cian Hughes’ 4-year-old gelding THOMPSON GUNNER, who has yet to make an impact in six turf starts. That said, his most recent run at the Curragh 27 days ago offered a glimmer of hope. Despite finishing 13th, for a brief moment half a furlong out, it looked like he might outrun his massive 50/1 odds and at least threaten the places. He eventually faded, finishing 7½ lengths behind, but it was far from a disgrace.
Now, this son of HIGHLAND REEL drops in grade, loses 3lbs, and gains the assistance of 5lb claimer Wayne Hassett - who boasts a strong 34.09% place strike rate here in Dublin over the past five years. That stat adds a layer of intrigue, especially as the gelding now runs 8lbs lighter overall.
While he may still be finding his feet, this looks a more winnable contest. It could be too early to expect fireworks, but there was enough in that last effort to suggest he might run better than the market expects once again.
A hope? A chance? Perhaps just enough of both to sneak into the frame this time.

Smaoineamh Sile recorded his 4th course and distance win with a bit in hand on last run - 3 of the wins on good or better so ground conditions ideal today. Would require career best having never won as high on this a mark but had the beating of a couple of these in last race and has alot in his favour to go well again
Harbanaker won over this C&D in April and remains well-treated on old form. He's unexposed at the trip, and with his proven course form, he's a strong contender to follow up.
Elusive Duke has been out of form but returned to form at Limerick just over a week ago, when he was backed very late. Has a chance here.

AMAVASYA is a three year old filly in open-age handicap company who merits close inspection. Her recent form at this venue was encouraging indeed and she should be open to considerable progress. Now with the yard among the recent winners she rates the value play.

Kartayaz has been consistently placing in his recent runs and shows good form on similar going. Despite a long losing streak, he's in the mix on these terms and can make his presence felt for an each-way bet.

Twice a winne over 1 mile for previous trainer who finished 5th over 1m1f here last week on soft ground behind todays predicted favourite Smaoineamh Sile. Will prefer this better ground and is 7lbs better off tonight so looks an eaxh way player with 5 places.

Here we are again with El Bello and even though i tipped this again lto, i mentioned that it would probably not be his day again and so it proved. I believe i also tipped the winner of that race as my other tip and was going to tip that again, but i think come race time the going might change from g/s to good and that will not help S Sile and also caught everyone napping lto which won't happen again. The market is a little strange atm as it seems to be favouring the horses that like it softer with the others drifting, but as i said that could all change by race time. El Bello has claimer DJ O'Connor back on top who was 3rd on him back in May and could be the difference today. Ew for betting and Gianh River is also a decent ew.

With 5 places available this looks excellent ew value.
With the jockeys 10lbs claim taken into account this horse can't really get any lower in the weights and was rated very substantially higher last year and further back.
Seems to go quite well with this jockey too.
This 9f distance will suit better than his last race although I would rather it was a longer distance.
Nevertheless,on these terms he can win this,especially as he has a history of reaching near to peak form at this time of year.

FERRYBANK caught the eye in a big way latest in behind those placed. He gets a relatively quick turnaround likely having found a suitable handicap opportunity for his shrewd trainer and sharper/ready now he makes maximum appeal.

A 3 times winner twice over this 7f trip who finished well into 4th over this CD last week beaaten around 2.5 lengths behind todays forecast Favourite Finsceal Annie. Has a 6lbs pull at the weights with that rival today so could well turn around the places.
Prince Of Eyeries won impressively last time out in a claimer, showing a strong turn of foot. Despite a wide draw, he's well-treated on his maiden form, contender.
Distance winner who comes here after poor run over much further last time out, looks on a handy mark if recapturing last seasons form

Yaxchilan won over six furlongs on good ground last time out and Chris Hayes has jumped ship from Punk Poet to this one, which could be a strong indication that this gelding is in fine fettle and could easily go in again.
Reliable sort, This horse is always thereabouts at the buisness end of races. Has trip and ground and a top jockey booking noted also.

It would be folly, in my opinion, to completely write off Michael Grassick’s 6-year-old mare AMANIRENAS here, especially sitting at the bottom of the weights. She steps back up to her preferred trip of 7f and returns to Leopardstown, where she’s run well in the past. She’s now a whopping 15lbs lower than her last winning mark - an eye-catching drop.
Now, you might be thinking, “Well, she’s obviously a stone lighter because she’s been running backwards,” and that’s a fair assumption. But it’s important to note this daughter of WAR COMMAND just hasn’t been running over her ideal distance. Five of her six best runs have come at 7f, and two of those came right here at Leopardstown.
Yes, she’s fallen in the handicap like a stone, but she didn’t disgrace herself last time out at Fairyhouse over 6f just 13 days ago. That effort on unsuitably short ground suggested there’s still life in her yet. The return to 7f, quicker ground, and the booking of Gavin Ryan - who holds a 25% place strike rate here over the past five years - all give cause for renewed optimism.
Overlook her completely and you might regret it.
Can show the benefit of a gentle racecourse introduction at Naas, and is fancied to turn the tables on the reopposing Battle Of Maldon, who finished in front of him in that trial at Naas.
Cost 37,000 euros as a yearling and sire was a top class middle distance horse. Can make a winning fist of this.
So Messi produced his best run of the season last time and has performed creditably over this C&D. He's worth an each-way bet if building on that recent encouraging effort.
Noble Andy has form in this grade, but over further distances. Is 3lb lower than when finishing 5th at Fairyhouse recently. Will take a chance he can deal with the lesser distance.
They are stepping this one back up to 9f with a 3lbs claiming jockey booking / change, a good value ew bet for the 5 places available.

SAYFA FAD was ridden by Colin Keane two starts back and went close having shown nothing prior to that effort. Presumably a racer who is pleasing connections , so back with a similar dynamic and ground to suit tonight the feeling is a big run will follow.
Horse has shown sings of improvement and with todays jockey claiming a handy 7 pounds, makes an attractive each way chance in this open looking contest.
Six times a winner on the all weather but has yet to strike on turf after twenty-nine attempts. A career low mark may enable him to gain that elusive first win on turf today.

TOMAHAWK KING should be capable as a five year old exploiting his current lowly handicap mark. He does not necessarily boast any strong form when fresh , but assuming the yard have him ready then he should be highly competitive. The market can provide further clues.

Certainly looks to be well in at the weights having dropped markedly down the handicap.
This.is a low grade race so anything near his best form should put him in the mix come the finish line.
5 places makes this a good value ew bet.
